items.prompt: Ice melts when it gets ___.

options.why: Cold keeps ice frozen.
Darkness does not melt ice. Warmth does.
Wind alone does not melt ice. Warmth does.

hints: Think about an ice cube in a hot drink.
What makes frozen things turn runny?
Picture ice in the sunshine. What happens to it?
items.explanation: Ice melts when it gets warm. The warmth turns the solid ice into liquid water.

items.prompt: What does ice turn into when it melts?

options.why: Ice is frozen water. When it melts, it becomes water again.
Steam comes from very hot water. Melting ice makes liquid water.
Glass is made by heating sand.

hints: Think about how ice cubes are made in a freezer.
What is left in a glass after the ice is gone?
Picture an ice cube on a plate. What is on the plate later?
items.explanation: Ice is frozen water. When it melts, it turns back into liquid water.

items.prompt: Match each action to the change it makes.
hints: Act out each action with your hands.
Which action makes something longer? Which makes it flatter?
Start with the rubber band. What happens when you pull it?
items.explanation: Pressing a sponge flat squashes it, wringing a towel twists it, pulling a rubber band stretches it and folding a pipe cleaner bends it.

items.prompt: Does it spring back or stay changed? Sort the cards.
hints: Some materials go back to their shape when you let go.
Imagine letting go of each one. Does it change back?
Start with the sponge. What happens when you stop squeezing?
items.explanation: A sponge, a rubber band and a spring go back to their shape. Clay, foil and dough stay in their new shape.

items.prompt: Putri leaves an ice lolly in the sun. What happens to it?

figure.alt: An ice lolly in the hot sun.

options.why: Heat makes ice softer, and then it melts.
A melting ice lolly gets smaller and runny.
The Sun's heat warms the ice lolly, so it changes.

hints: What happens to frozen things when they get warm?
Picture holding an ice lolly at the beach.
items.explanation: The heat from the Sun warms the ice lolly and it melts into a runny liquid.

items.prompt: Water turns into ice in a freezer. We say the water ___.
hints: The name of the freezer gives a clue.
Say it aloud: the freezer makes water ___.
items.explanation: When water gets very cold it freezes and becomes solid ice. Melting is the opposite change.

items.prompt: Which change can be undone?

options.why: A baked cake cannot turn back into runny cake mix.
A cooked egg cannot become runny again.
Burnt paper cannot become paper again.

hints: Think about what happens when each thing cools down again.
Can you get the material back the way it was?
Ask: what happens to melted chocolate in the fridge?
items.explanation: Melted chocolate sets hard again when it cools, so the change can be undone. Baking, cooking and burning cannot be undone.

items.prompt: Choose all the things that melt when they get warm.

options.why: A stone stays hard in the sun.
Wood does not melt in the sun.

hints: Think about what happens on a hot day.
Which things become soft and runny?
Start with chocolate. What happens to it in a warm pocket?
items.explanation: Ice, chocolate and butter melt when they get warm. A stone and a wooden spoon stay solid.

items.prompt: Leo squashes a ball of plasticine and lets go. What happens?

options.text: It springs back into a ball.
options.why: Plasticine keeps its new shape. A sponge would spring back.
Squashing changes the shape. It does not melt the plasticine.
Squashing changes the shape. The plasticine is the same amount.

hints: Think about playing with plasticine or clay.
Does plasticine go back to its old shape?
Compare it with a sponge. What is different?
items.explanation: Plasticine stays in its new squashed shape. Some materials, like sponges, spring back, but plasticine does not.

items.prompt: Mira pulls both ends of a rubber band. What is she doing?

figure.alt: A rubber band being pulled at both ends.

options.why: Squashing pushes something together. Mira is pulling.
Melting needs heat. Mira is pulling.
Freezing needs cold. Mira is pulling.

hints: Pulling both ends makes it longer.
Which word means making something longer by pulling?
Act it out with your hands.
items.explanation: Pulling both ends stretches the rubber band. It gets longer and goes back when she lets go.

items.prompt: Put the steps for making an ice lolly in order.
items: Put the mould in the freezer.
Wait for the juice to freeze.
hints: You need the juice in something before it can freeze.
The freezer does the cold part.
Start with the juice. Where does it go first?
items.explanation: Pour the juice into a mould, put it in the freezer and wait for it to freeze. Then take out the ice lolly.

items.prompt: Butter is hard in the fridge. Ani leaves it out on a hot day. What happens?

options.why: Warmth makes butter softer.

options.text: It becomes soft and may melt.

options.why: Freezing needs cold. The day is hot.
Butter changes when it warms up.

hints: Think about the difference between the fridge and a hot day.
What does warmth do to butter?
Picture spreading butter straight from the fridge, then on a hot day.
items.explanation: Warmth makes butter soft, and on a very hot day it can melt. Putting it back in the fridge makes it hard again.

items.prompt: A puddle of melted ice is put back in the freezer. What happens?

figure.alt: A puddle of water going into a freezer.

options.text: It stays as water for ever.
options.why: Freezing turns water into ice again.
Steam comes from very hot water.
The water is still there. It changes into ice.

hints: A freezer makes things very cold.
What happens to water when it gets very cold?
Think about how ice cubes are made.
items.explanation: The cold freezer turns the water back into ice. Melting and freezing can be undone.

items.prompt: Water freezes at 0 °C. Would ice melt or stay frozen in this room?

figure.alt: A thermometer showing 25 degrees Celsius in the room.

options.why: 25 °C is much warmer than 0 °C, so the ice melts.
Ice does not grow in a warm room.

options.text: It would turn into steam straight away.
options.why: Water needs to be much hotter to turn into steam.

hints: Read the number on the thermometer first.
Ask: is the room warmer or colder than freezing?
items.explanation: The room is 25 °C, which is much warmer than 0 °C. Ice warms up and melts in this room.

items.prompt: Which one shows heating changing a material for ever?

options.why: Water can freeze back into ice, so this can be undone.
Melted chocolate can set hard again.
Soft butter goes hard again in the fridge.

hints: For ever means it cannot be changed back.
Think about cooling each one down again.
Ask: can toast ever become soft bread again?
items.explanation: Toasting changes bread for ever. Cooling toast does not turn it back into bread. Melting can be undone by cooling.

items.prompt: Can the change be undone? Sort the cards.
hints: Undone means you can get the material back as it was.
Start with the cooked egg. Can it ever be runny again?
items.explanation: Melting ice, freezing water and squashing a sponge can be undone. Baking, cooking and burning make new materials, so they cannot be undone.

items.prompt: Draw a ball of clay before and after you squash it. Label each picture.

criteria.label: Draws the clay as a round ball
Draws the clay flat after squashing

hints: Draw the ball first, then the flat shape next to it.
Add an arrow between them to show the squash.
items.explanation: Squashing is a push. It changes the clay from a round ball into a flat shape, and the clay stays flat.

items.prompt: How can you change the shape of clay?

options.why: Singing does not change it.
Looking does not change it.
It stays the same.

items.explanation: We can squash, roll or pinch clay to change its shape.

items.prompt: What happens to chocolate in the hot sun?

options.why: Heat does not freeze things.
It does not grow.
That cannot happen.

items.explanation: Heat from the Sun melts chocolate.

items.prompt: Which one cannot be changed back?

options.why: Water can freeze again.
It springs back.
It goes back.

hints: Think about things that go back.
items.explanation: Toast burns for ever. It cannot go back into bread.

items.prompt: A puddle dries up on a hot day. Where has the water gone?

options.why: Some soaks in, but heat also dries it.
It does not go there.
It becomes a gas in the air.

items.explanation: Heat turns the water into an invisible gas that goes into the air. This is called evaporation.

items.prompt: What happens when a cake bakes in a hot oven?

options.why: It cannot do that.

options.text: Heat changes the mixture for ever.

options.why: Heat does not make ice.
The mixture becomes a cake.

items.explanation: Baking changes the mixture into a cake. We cannot turn the cake back into the mixture.

items.prompt: Which change is caused by cooling?

options.why: That is melting, from heat.
That is from heat.
That is from heat.

items.explanation: When water gets very cold it freezes into ice.

items.prompt: Bread is made into toast. Can the toast become bread again?

options.text: No, toasting changes it for ever.

options.why: Cooling does not change it back.
It does not turn into bread again.
Squashing does not help.

items.explanation: Toasting is a change that cannot be undone.

items.prompt: Is it caused by heating or cooling? Sort the changes.
items.explanation: Ice cream and chocolate melt when heated and water boils when heated. Water freezes, jelly sets and a puddle turns to ice when cooled.

items.prompt: How is the shape changed? Sort the actions.
items.explanation: Pressing squashes. Pulling stretches. Wringing and turning twist.

items.prompt: Choose all the changes that cannot be undone.
items.explanation: Baking, burning and frying change materials for ever. Melted ice can freeze again and a sponge springs back.

items.prompt: Match each material to how we can change its shape.
items.explanation: We squash clay, stretch elastic, bend wire and twist a towel.

items.prompt: Put the steps for making toast in order.
items.explanation: We put bread in the toaster and wait for the heat. Then we take it out and spread butter.

items.prompt: Heating can ___ ice. Cooling can ___ water.
items.explanation: Heating melts ice and cooling freezes water.

items.prompt: What happens?
head: Action
Result
hints: Dough is cooked in an oven.
items.explanation: Heated chocolate melts. Cooled water freezes. Baked dough goes hard and cooks.

items.prompt: Putri puts a lolly in the Sun. It starts to melt. She puts it back in the freezer. It goes hard again.

parts.prompt: What makes the lolly hard again?

items.explanation: The Sun's heat melts the lolly. The cold freezer makes it hard again.

items.prompt: Ice melts in 8 minutes in the Sun. In the shade it takes 15 minutes. How many more minutes in the shade?
hints: The shade is cooler, so it takes longer.
items.explanation: 15 - 8 = 7 more minutes in the shade.

items.prompt: Tap the thing that melts in the Sun.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: ice cream, rock, spoon and key.

hints: Which one is cold and soft?
Metal does not melt in the Sun.
items.explanation: Ice cream melts when it gets warm. Rocks, spoons and keys do not melt in the Sun.

items.prompt: When ice melts, it turns into ___.
hints: Think about what is in a puddle.
items.explanation: Ice is frozen water. When it melts it turns back into water.

items.prompt: Draw an ice cream before and after it melts in the Sun.
items.explanation: In the Sun, ice cream melts and becomes runny. We call the two pictures before and after.

items.prompt: Ice cubes sit in a freezer, a classroom and the hot Sun. Which does not melt?

options.why: It is warm enough to melt.

options.text: the one in the hot Sun
options.why: The Sun melts ice.
The freezer is below 0 degrees.

items.explanation: The freezer is colder than 0 degrees, so the ice stays frozen.

items.prompt: Ben bakes a clay bowl in a hot oven. Can he make the bowl soft again by squashing it?

options.text: No, baking changed it for ever.

options.why: Baked clay stays hard.
Waiting does not help.
It does not go back.

items.explanation: Baking makes the clay hard for ever. Squashing will not make it soft again.

items.prompt: Which cannot be undone?

options.why: The sponge dries again.
It can set again.
It can be straightened.

hints: A pipe cleaner can be straightened.
items.explanation: A burnt match is changed for ever. The other changes can be undone.
